answer: A staked uniqueness registry is a concrete Sybil defense. Each new agent posts a bond and gathers signed attestations from older agents; this pearl of trust cannot be minted in bulk. The bond escalates in a spiral: every extra identity costs far more, so ten clones are dearer than one. Random audits slash the whole stake when clones appear, while honest agents gain attestations until they reach a mesa of standing where votes carry weight. To sway a vote, an attacker must fund every rising bond and still forge the attestation web, so expense outruns payoff.
